provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: Mechanism: count every cell that is not the background colour, then output a strip of length N filled with the single foreground colour. In the original family the background is 0 and the output is common.grid(N, 1, color), which is 1 row by N columns. Under the palette map the background becomes the constant palette[0]. The emitted program compares cells against that constant. It does not use a majority-colour heuristic, because a dense input such as the 5-vs-4 test, or a full 9-cell grid, would fool one. The foreground colour is read from the visible non-background pixels. Under D4, a uniform 1xN row stays a row when the clockwise rotation count d4%4 is even, and the row reversal for indices >= 4 has no effect on a uniform row. It becomes an N x 1 column when the rotation count is odd. The emitted program writes that strip directly in visible coordinates. The input grid is 3x3 and only its cell count matters, so the input needs no orientation handling.
draft_notes.limitations: Assumes the palette is a permutation of colours. random_color() in the constructor never returns 0, so the foreground always differs from palette[0]. The generator always places 1-9 pixels of a single colour. The n==0 fallback (returning a 1x1 background cell) and the smallest-colour tie-break when several foreground colours are present are defensive only and lie outside the constructor's domain. I found no constructor defects. The fixtures match the uniform rule; note that the validate() train order differs from the fixture order, which is harmless. No tests were run.

independent_source_review.mechanism: Count the cells that differ from the fixed background palette[0] in the 3x3 input, then output a uniform strip of the single foreground colour with length N. The strip is 1xN when the D4 rotation count is even and Nx1 when it is odd.
evidence: Constructor: count = common.randint(1, 9) and common.sample(all_pixels(3,3), count) give distinct pixels, so len(rows) equals the number of coloured cells. color = common.random_color() draws from range(1,10), so it is never 0.

Output: common.grid(len(rows), 1, color). In common.py, grid(width, height, color) builds `height` rows of `width` cells, so the output is 1 row by N columns. This matches the fixtures: [[7]], [[2,2,2]], [[8,8,8,8]], [[1,1]] and [[4,4,4,4,4]].
The fixture inputs agree with validate(): counts 1, 3, 4 and 2, and a test count of 5 for colour 4. Only the train order differs, which is harmless.

Factory: mask = g != BG with BG = palette[0] is an explicit background constant. It is correct on the dense 5-vs-4 test and on a full 9-cell grid, where a majority-background guess would fail. The archived program also uses g != 0 explicitly.

The colour is read from the visible non-background pixels. In-domain there is exactly one such colour, so the min tie-break is never used. There is no hidden latent and no arbitrary lookup association; the colour is copied from the query itself.

Orientation: a uniform strip is invariant under reflection and is only transposed by odd quarter-turns. VERTICAL = (d4 % 4) % 2 == 1 writes [[c]]*N as a column directly in visible coordinates. No whole-grid untransform/retransform wrapper is used.
The input orientation is irrelevant because only the cell count matters.
Host audit: passed, with 1000 fresh pairs, 8000 augmented checks, 16 fixture variants and no sampler rejections.
nonblocking_limits: The n == 0 fallback [[BG]] and the smallest-colour tie-break when several foreground colours appear are outside the constructor's domain (count >= 1, single colour) and are defensive only.
The solver assumes the palette is a permutation, so the mapped foreground never equals palette[0]. This holds because random_color excludes 0.
The demonstrations argument is unused. This is acceptable because the rule needs no episode-specific association.
The input is always 3x3. Grid size does not affect the solver.
required_context_checks: Confirm that the host D4 indexing has 4..7 as reflection composed with rotation (d4 % 4 quarter-turns), so that odd d4 maps a 1xN row to an Nx1 column for every index. The 8000 augmented checks, with d4 = 7 sampled, appear to cover all 8 variants.
d631b094 is not in the require_colour_evidence task list. None is needed, since the output colour comes directly from the query input.
